data.title: Oil prices fall amid equity selloff though Iran war attacks limit losses
data.description:
PERTH, Nov 23 (Reuters) - Oil prices fell on Monday as the selloff in the wider financial markets amid concerns about the ability of the AI sector to boost economic growth spilled over into commodities, though the continuing attacks on Gulf shipping limited the losses.

Crude dropped, adding to its three-week losing streak, amid the overall negative sentiment in global financial markets as Asian equities opened lower on Monday, with the tech-heavy South Korean market down 4% and China, Hong Kong and Australia all falling. US equity markets have also slumped with the Nasdaq plunging 10% last week.

Brent crude futures fell 28 cents, or 0.30%, to $92.29 a barrel by 0216 GMT. US West Texas Intermediate futures fell 15 cents, or 0.18%, to $83.26 a barrel. 

Brent declined 4% last week and WTI 5%.

Still, the fighting from the unresolved US-Israeli war against Iran continues to limit any losses. On Sunday, the Iran-aligned Houthi movement claimed it attacked a Saudi Arabian oil refinery and over the weekend multiple attacks on shipping in the Gulf and near the Strait of Hormuz were reported. 

"It's momentum carrying (oil) down," said Mukesh Sahdev, chief oil analyst at Sydney-based XAnalysts. But he cautioned that the shipping attacks are having an effect as "ballast (empty) vessels counts are building in crude while laden vessels are not. This risk to flows will start to price soon."

In Turkey, talks on Sunday at the global climate summit COP31 collapsed for the first time since 2009 after nations could not come to an agreement over including a statement on the phase-out of fossil fuels in a final text. 

Saudi Arabia and other big oil-producing countries have said fossil fuels will play a role in the economy for the foreseeable future and they lobbied to keep any mention of fossil fuels out of the text, observers at the summit said. 

OPEC had earlier defended fossil fuel use at the summit.

OPEC+ ministers will hold a series of meetings on November 29 to decide their 2027 output policy. The group comprises the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries and allies such as Russia.

(Reporting by Helen Clark; Editing by Christian Schmollinger)

data.title: Alice Huang in touch with Chinese spy agency during affair with Nvidia CEO, NYT says
data.description:
WASHINGTON, Nov 22 (Reuters) - Alice Huang, the Chinese woman at the heart of Nvidia's ( NVDA ) recent scandal, kept in contact with an official from China's top spy agency for more than a year during her affair with former CEO Jensen Huang, the New York Times reported on Sunday.

Alice Huang was in touch with an officer from China's Ministry of State Security from the spring of 2025 until the fall of this year, the report said, citing people with knowledge of intelligence reports that describe the encounters.

Spokespersons for Nvidia ( NVDA ), Jensen Huang and the Chinese Embassy in Washington did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Reuters has not been able to reach Alice Huang for comment.

Alice Huang previously led Singapore-based Megaspeed International, an important Nvidia ( NVDA ) customer that once accounted for billions in Nvidia ( NVDA ) chip sales.

US authorities have been investigating Megaspeed since 2024 over concerns it smuggled Nvidia's ( NVDA ) advanced AI chips to China.

Sunday's report comes as US officials have cast doubt on initial suggestions that Alice Huang was a spy, as the newspaper reported last month.

That October 29 article touched off a scandal that led to Jensen Huang's resignation two weeks later and a steep drop in Nvidia's ( NVDA ) stock price.

Trump administration officials have repeatedly said they have not concluded that Alice Huang spied for China.

US Attorney General Todd Blanche said this month the Justice Department had not yet reached a conclusion on whether she was a Chinese spy.

US Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton repeated that on Sunday.

"Attorney General Blanche has been very clear that this is a matter under investigation, both Ms Huang and her company, for various matters," Clayton told CNN's "State of the Union" program. "And I'm going to let that investigation play out."

The scandal has also prompted a deeper look at Washington's approach to export controls on China, with lawmakers from both parties questioning whether the Trump administration has been too lax on enforcement and regulation of the prized semiconductors.

The affair between the two itself is of less interest, Senator John Kennedy, a Louisiana Republican, told NBC's "Meet the Press."

"I hope he had a good time," Kennedy said on Sunday. "It was the most expensive sex since Helen of Troy."

(Reporting by Alexandra Alper; Additional reporting by Katharine Jackson; Editing by Sergio Non and Lincoln Feast.)

data.title: US futures bounce while Asia markets brace for AI wipeout
data.description:
SINGAPORE, Nov 23 (Reuters) - US stock futures attempted a recovery on Monday, while Asian markets slid and authorities around the region readied support measures after a withering wipeout last week for tech and chip stocks at the centre of the AI boom.

Investors are questioning whether the vast sums of mostly borrowed money spent building data centres to power AI models will generate returns fast enough to repay lenders and big enough to justify some of the high stock prices.

Last week's 10% drop in the Nasdaq was its largest weekly drop since pandemic panic gripped markets in March 2020.

Nasdaq 100 futures bounced nearly 3% in early trade on Monday, and S&P 500 futures rose by 2%.

South Korea's chip-heavy KOSPI dropped more than 3% in the first few minutes of morning trade.

Japan markets are closed for a holiday on Monday but futures indicate selling pressure, while Hang Seng futures also point to a fall. Australian stocks were slightly lower.

The "AI trade" has for several years lifted a wide range of stocks, from switch and cable makers to electricity generators and the manufacturers of anything in the computing supply chain, but they have been under pressure in recent months from rising interest rates. [.N]

AI-related shares took a particularly sharp downturn last week as the exit of Jensen Huang, the Nvidia ( NVDA ) CEO nicknamed the "godfather of AI", and the faltering debut of AI company Anthropic, which closed 8.5% lower on its first full day of trading, pointed to a souring mood.

Taiwanese shares were down 17% for the week, their biggest weekly fall since 1990, and Friday's 10% drop for the Philadelphia semiconductor index points to more pain for Asia's chip-heavy markets, especially in Taiwan and South Korea.

Taiwan's financial regulator on Saturday ordered a further tightening of short-selling rules for stocks, while in China stock exchanges announced a batch of support measures such as easing requirements for margin financing.

South Korea will be ready to deploy market stabilisation funds immediately should the market continue to fall, the finance ministry said on Sunday, after the benchmark index last week slumped to 10-month lows.

(Reporting by Tom Westbrook; Editing by Edmund Klamann)

data.title: Australia shares set to slide at open, NZ falls
data.description:
Nov 23 (Reuters) - Australian shares were poised to open lower on Monday, with miners likely to take a hit from weaker copper and gold prices, while sentiment remained fragile after last week's soft jobs data stoked fears of a sharp economic slowdown.

The local share price index futures fell 0.6%, a 36.6-point discount to the underlying S&P/ASX 200 index close. The benchmark fell 1.6% on Friday.

New Zealand's benchmark S&P/NZX 50 index fell 1% in early trade.

(Reporting by Shravya Marakini in Bengaluru; Editing by Edmund Klamann)

data.title: Zepp Health Corporation Reports Third Quarter of 2026 Unaudited Financial Results
data.description:
MILPITAS, Calif., Nov. 22, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Zepp Health Corporation ( ZEPP ) ("Zepp", the "Company" or "we") today announced its unaudited financial results for the third quarter of 2026.

Third Quarter of 2026 Financial and Operating Highlights:

  • Revenue reached US$68.3 million, representing a year-over-year decrease of 9.9% and a quarter-over-quarter increase of 7.5%.
  • Gross margin was 35.0%, compared with 38.2% and 37.4% in the same period of 2025 and the second quarter of 2026, respectively. Gross margin faced several headwinds during the quarter, primarily elevated memory and other component costs, as well as foreign currency impacts. While product mix improved year-over-year, this favorable mix benefit was more than offset by higher memory costs within our entry-level price segments.
  • GAAP and adjusted net loss[1] attributable to Zepp were US$12.6 million and US$11.6 million, respectively, compared with US$1.6 million and US$0.7 million in the same period of 2025, and US$11.3 million and US$12.5 million in the second quarter of 2026. The net loss was due to lower gross margin mainly resulting from higher memory and other component costs and foreign currency headwinds, as well as increased investment in marketing and branding activities.
  • As of September 30, 2026, cash and cash equivalents and restricted cash totaled US$99.0 million, compared with US$102.6 million as of September 30, 2025 and US$106.3 million as of June 30, 2026.
  • Product Innovation: Launched T-Rex Dual Solar, pairing a bright AMOLED display with solar charging through both the front of the watch and its glass-ceramic back. It offers up to 25 days of battery life under typical use, and its dual-sided solar charging and offline navigation are designed for multi-day trips outdoors.
  • Software Ecosystem: Rolled out Zepp OS 6 to more existing watch models and made HYROX post-race station analysis available on more models. These updates give customers more value from the devices they already own and help build confidence in Amazfit's ongoing support for its products.

[1] Adjusted net income/(loss) attributable to Zepp Health Corporation ( ZEPP ) represents net income/(loss) excluding (i) share-based compensation expenses, (ii) amortization of intangible assets resulting from acquisitions and business cooperation agreements, (iii) gain/(loss) from fair value change of long-term investments, (iv) impairment loss from long-term investments, (v) income/(loss) from equity method investments, (vi) investment income/(loss) and (vii) tax effects of the above non-GAAP adjustments. See "Reconciliation of GAAP and Non-GAAP Results" at the end of this press release.

"The third quarter was a period of adjustment for us," said Wayne Huang, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Zepp Health ( ZEPP ). "Tight supply for some of our core products weighed on revenue, while unfavorable exchange rates and higher prices for memory and other chips put pressure on gross margin. The adjustments we made across our products, training software, supply, and retail are already beginning to pay off in the fourth quarter, and we are heading into the holiday season and the year ahead with momentum.

In the third quarter, global activations across the Balance family rose approximately 40% from the second quarter, driven by our new, higher-priced models. Combined global activations for Active 3 Premium and Active Max, our two US$169 models, grew approximately 35% over the same period. We also expanded our premium outdoor lineup with T-Rex Dual Solar, a watch priced at about US$650 that pairs a bright AMOLED display with dual-sided solar charging and offline navigation for multi-day trips. Through Zepp OS 6 and HYROX updates, we brought new training tools to more watches that customers already own, giving them more value from their devices.

Product availability has started to improve in some markets in the fourth quarter, including for T-Rex 3. We have also made it easier for customers to compare watches in stores. At REI, we provided materials to help shoppers compare models. Large screens are now in place at our Amazfit counters in select Best Buy stores. They make the counters easier to spot and show shoppers how our devices fit into everyday activity, training, and recovery. As more products reach store shelves, we believe we will be better positioned to meet holiday demand."

Leon Deng, Chief Financial Officer of Zepp Health ( ZEPP ), commented, "Third-quarter revenue reached US$68.3 million, up 7.5% sequentially and within our guidance range. While revenue declined 9.9% year-over-year, we continued to see encouraging momentum in our Active series. Supply constraints on certain higher-margin products, including Balance 3 and Helio Strap, limited our ability to fully capture market demand during the quarter.

Gross margin was 35.0%, compared with 37.4% in the previous quarter and 38.2% in the same period last year, reflecting unfavorable foreign exchange movements, continued increases in memory component costs, and supply constraints on our higher-margin products. Importantly, excluding the tariff-related benefit recorded in the second quarter, our underlying gross margin remained strong sequentially. Continued improvement in our product mix helped offset a meaningful portion of these external cost pressures, demonstrating the progress we have made in strengthening our premium product portfolio and underlying unit economics.

We continued to balance financial discipline with targeted investments to support future growth. On a sequential basis, adjusted operating expenses decreased to US$34.2 million, and adjusted operating loss narrowed to US$10.3 million. The year-over-year increase in operating expenses was primarily driven by strategic investments in new product launches, brand building, athlete partnerships, and distribution expansion. At the same time, general and administrative expenses declined, reflecting our ongoing efforts to improve operational efficiency and manage our structural cost base.

We ended the quarter with US$99.0 million in cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash, while inventory declined to US$68.6 million from US$87.7 million a year earlier. We also continued to strengthen our balance sheet by extending our debt maturity profile, converting an additional US$26.6 million of short-term borrowings into longer-term obligations during the quarter. We remain committed to returning value to shareholders through our ongoing share repurchase program. As of September 30, 2026, we had cumulatively repurchased US$17.8 million under our US$20 million authorization, and our board of directors recently approved a one-year extension of the existing program.

Looking ahead, we expect fourth-quarter revenue to be between US$90.0 million and US$95.0 million, representing year-over-year growth of approximately 6% to 12%. As product availability improves and our expanded distribution channels begin contributing more meaningfully, we remain focused on translating our investments into stronger revenue growth and greater operating leverage. Despite near-term external cost pressures, we believe our improving product mix, disciplined cost management, and continued investment in the Amazfit brand are building a stronger foundation for sustainable long-term growth and profitability."

Third Quarter of 2026 Financial Results

Revenues

Revenue reached US$68.3 million, representing a year-over-year decrease of 9.9% and a quarter-over-quarter increase of 7.5%. The year-over-year decline was due to the broader macroeconomic environment and a strong comparison base, as well as supply constraints on top-selling offerings, particularly Helio Strap and Balance 3. However, revenue from the Active series increased significantly year-over-year.

Gross Margin

Gross margin was 35.0%, compared with 38.2% and 37.4% in the same period of 2025 and the second quarter of 2026, respectively. Gross margin faced several headwinds during the quarter, primarily elevated memory and other component costs, as well as foreign currency impacts. While product mix improved year-over-year, supported by new product introductions including the Active series, this favorable mix benefit was more than offset by higher memory costs within our entry-level price segments. Gross margin for the second quarter of 2026 benefited from tariff refunds that the Company recorded related to duties previously remitted under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act ("IEEPA"). Excluding the impact of these refunds, gross margin increased sequentially.

Research and Development Expenses

Research and development expenses in the third quarter of 2026 were US$11.4 million, compared with US$10.8 million and US$11.5 million in the third quarter of 2025 and the second quarter of 2026, respectively. Excluding US$0.6 million of foreign currency headwinds, research and development expenses were flat compared with the same period of 2025. We continued to invest in a series of cutting-edge products as well as new technologies, including AI, to maintain our competitive edge against our peers. At the same time, we focused on refined research and development approaches, consistently evaluating resource efficiency to optimize return on investment and productivity.

Selling and Marketing Expenses

Selling and marketing expenses in the third quarter of 2026 were US$18.0 million, compared with US$12.0 million and US$18.3 million in the third quarter of 2025 and the second quarter of 2026, respectively. The US$6.0 million year-over-year increase was primarily attributable to US$1.9 million investment across online and offline channels for content refreshes, in-store displays and holiday season readiness, and US$1.5 million of launch campaigns for new products including the Balance 3, Balance Ultra and T-Rex Dual Solar. The remainder of the increase reflected US$1.4 million for marathons, Ultra-Trail du Mont-Blanc (UTMB) and media sponsorships, and US$1.2 million related to the HYROX and new athletes partnerships.

General and Administrative Expenses

General and administrative expenses were US$5.6 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared with US$7.0 million and US$6.2 million in the third quarter of 2025 and the second quarter of 2026, respectively. We continued to streamline overhead, maintaining disciplined cost control while improving operating efficiency.

Operating Expenses

GAAP and adjusted operating expenses[2] for the third quarter of 2026 were US$35.0 million and US$34.2 million, respectively, compared with US$29.8 million and US$28.6 million in the third quarter of 2025, and US$36.0 million and US$34.8 million in the second quarter of 2026. Out of the year-over-year increase of US$5.2 million in operating expenses, US$0.8 million was due to foreign currency impacts. The remaining US$4.4 million was primarily due to higher selling and marketing expenses as mentioned above. On a quarter-over-quarter basis, operating expenses decreased slightly.

Operating Income/(Loss)

GAAP and adjusted operating results[3] were loss of US$11.1 million and loss of US$10.3 million, respectively, compared with loss of US$0.9 million and income of US$0.4 million in the same quarter of 2025. The net operating loss was due to lower gross margin mainly resulting from higher memory and other component costs and foreign currency headwinds, as well as increased investment in marketing and branding activities, but the operating loss narrowed compared with the second quarter of 2026. 

Net Income/(Loss)

GAAP and adjusted net loss attributable to Zepp for the third quarter of 2026 were US$12.6 million and US$11.6 million, respectively, compared with GAAP and adjusted net loss of US$1.6 million and US$0.7 million for the same quarter in 2025. The US$10.9 million year-over-year increase in adjusted net loss was primarily driven by a US$6.0 million increase in selling and marketing expenses, as discussed above, followed by a US$3.2 million unfavorable foreign exchange impact. In addition, higher memory and other component costs resulted in a net US$2.7 million gross profit headwind, partially mitigated by a more favorable product mix. These unfavorable impacts were partially offset by US$1.1 million in savings from general and administrative expenses.

[2] Adjusted operating expenses represent operating expenses excluding (i) share-based compensation expenses and (ii) amortization of intangible assets resulting from acquisitions and business cooperation agreements. Please refer to the section titled "Reconciliation of GAAP and Non-GAAP Results" at the end of this press release.

[3] Adjusted operating income/(loss) represents operating income/(loss) excluding: (i) share-based compensation expenses and (ii) amortization of intangible assets resulting from acquisitions and business cooperation agreements. See "Reconciliation of GAAP and Non-GAAP Results" at the end of this press release.

Liquidity and Capital Resources

As of September 30, 2026, cash and cash equivalents and restricted cash were US$99.0 million, compared with US$102.6 million and US$106.3 million as of September 30, 2025 and June 30, 2026, respectively.

The Company recorded inventory of US$68.6 million as of September 30, 2026, compared with US$62.4 million as of June 30, 2026 and US$87.7 million as of September 30, 2025. We will continue to manage the inventory level tightly and working capital closely.

Long-term and short-term debt levels remained flat as of September 30, 2026 compared with June 30, 2026. We remain committed to prudently managing our debt profile. Our primary objective is to maintain overall debt levels broadly stable while actively extending the maturity profile by replacing short-term borrowings with long-term debt. During the third quarter and for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, we successfully converted US$26.6 million and US$56.5 million, respectively, of short-term debt into long-term obligations, and we expect to continue this strategy in the coming quarters, supported by sufficient financial headroom and liquidity capacity. Since the beginning of 2023, the Company has cumulatively retired US$38.1 million of debt, and will continue to optimize its capital structure.

Share Repurchase Program Update

The Company announced in its third quarter 2021 earnings release that the board had authorized a share repurchase program of up to US$20 million through November 2022. On November 21, 2022, the board authorized a 12-month extension of the Company's share repurchase program. On November 20, 2023, the board further authorized the Company to extend its share repurchase program for another 12 months. On November 18, 2024, the board further authorized the Company to extend its share repurchase program for another 24 months. On November 22, 2026, the board further authorized the Company to extend its share repurchase program for another 12 months. Pursuant to the extended share repurchase program, the Company may repurchase its shares in the form of ADSs and/or ordinary shares through November 2027 with an aggregate value equal to the remaining balance under the share repurchase program. As of September 30, 2026, the Company had used US$17.8 million to repurchase approximately 2.4 million ADSs. The Company expects to fund the repurchases under the extended share repurchase program out of its existing cash balance.

Outlook

For the fourth quarter of 2026, the Company's management currently expects net revenues to be between US$90.0 million and US$95.0 million, which would represent an increase by approximately 6% to 12% from US$85.2 million in the fourth quarter of 2025.

This outlook is based on current market conditions and reflects the Company's current and preliminary estimates of market, operating conditions and customer demand, which are all subject to change.

About Zepp Health Corporation ( ZEPP )

Zepp Health ( ZEPP ) is the technology company behind Amazfit, a global sports technology brand. Its wider portfolio includes Zepp Clarity hearing technology and Zepp Aura sleep and recovery services.

The company's vertically integrated technology platform brings together Zepp OS, wearable chipsets and biometric sensors designed in-house, and algorithms for biometric measurement and personalized guidance to enhance product performance and user experiences across devices, software and services.

Zepp Health ( ZEPP ) operates as a global multi-hub organization, bringing together R&D, product, design, brand and business expertise across the Americas, Europe and Asia. These teams co-create and share responsibility for innovation, product performance and global growth.

Founded in 2013, Zepp Health ( ZEPP ) has shipped more than 200 million units of smart wearable devices, with products available in more than 90 countries. Its principal office is in Gorinchem, the Netherlands. For more information, visit: www.zepp.com

Use of Non-GAAP Measures

Adjusted operating expenses represent operating expenses excluding (i) share-based compensation expenses and (ii) amortization of intangible assets resulting from acquisitions and business cooperation agreements. Adjusted operating income/(loss) represents operating income/(loss) excluding: (i) share-based compensation expenses and (ii) amortization of intangible assets resulting from acquisitions and business cooperation agreements. Adjusted EBIT represents net income/(loss) excluding (i) share-based compensation expenses, (ii) amortization of intangible assets resulting from acquisitions and business cooperation agreements, (iii) gain/(loss) from fair value change of long-term investments, (iv) impairment loss from long-term investments, (v) income/(loss) from equity method investments, (vi) investment income/(loss), (vii) income tax (benefit)/expense, and (viii) interest income and interest expense. Adjusted net income/(loss) attributable to Zepp Health Corporation ( ZEPP ) is a non-GAAP measure, which excludes (i) share-based compensation expenses, (ii) amortization of intangible assets resulting from acquisitions and business cooperation agreements, (iii) gain/(loss) from fair value change of long-term investments, (iv) impairment loss from long-term investments, (v) income/(loss) from equity method investments, (vi) investment income/(loss), and (vii) tax effects of the above non-GAAP adjustments, and is used as the numerator in computation of adjusted net income/(loss) per share and per ADS attributable to Zepp Health Corporation ( ZEPP ).

We believe that adjusted EBIT and adjusted net income/(loss) attributable to Zepp Health Corporation ( ZEPP ) help identify underlying trends in our business that could otherwise be distorted by the effect of certain expenses that we include in net income/(loss) and net income/(loss) attributable to Zepp Health Corporation ( ZEPP ). We believe adjusted EBIT and adjusted net income/(loss) attributable to Zepp Health Corporation ( ZEPP ) provide useful information about our operating results, enhance the overall understanding of our past performance and future prospects and allow for greater visibility with respect to key metrics used by our management in its financial and operational decision-making.

Adjusted EBIT and adjusted net income/(loss) attributable to Zepp Health Corporation ( ZEPP ), should not be considered in isolation or construed as an alternative to net income/(loss), basic and diluted net income/(loss) per share and per ADS attributable to Zepp Health Corporation ( ZEPP ) or any other measure of performance or as an indicator of our operating performance. Other companies may calculate similarly titled measures differently, limiting their usefulness as comparative measures to our data. data.title: Libya's NOC says 'unlawful' pipeline closure from Sharara oilfield to cut output by 350,000 bpd
data.description:
Nov 23 (Reuters) - Libya's National Oil Corporation (NOC) said on Monday the closure of a valve on a pipeline from the Sharara oilfield, one of Libya's largest, by an "unlawful group" would result in the loss of around 350,000 barrels per day (bpd) of production.

A second pipeline, linking the Hamada field to the country's largest refinery, Zawiya, has also remained closed for more than two weeks, resulting in the loss of around 15,000 bpd, the NOC said, bringing Libya's total oil production losses to approximately 365,000 bpd.

The NOC said in October that an armed group had shut a valve on the main Hamada crude oil pipeline, halting flows. The Corporation said on Saturday that the forced closure of the Hamada oil pipeline had cost the country more than $30.8 million, renewing its condemnation of attacks on oil facilities.

Located ​in southwestern Libya, Sharara ​is operated ⁠by a joint venture of the state-owned NOC via Acacus oil company with Spain's Repsol, France's TotalEnergies, Austria's ​OMV and Norway's Equinor ( EQNR ).

Libyan oil output has been subject to repeated closures for political ​and technical reasons since the 2011 uprising against Muammar Gaddafi.

Oil production is Libya's main economic resource, representing ​approximately 90% ⁠of its economy.

(Reporting by Yomna Ehab; Editing by Tom Hogue and Lincoln Feast.)

data.title: AIPro Releases Free Version of 'VistaPro' AI Fire Early-Detection Software, Working with Existing CCTV
data.description:
Download requires no sign-up; basic features available with no time limit; includes 1 AI detection channel and 2 general monitoring channels

SEOUL, South Korea, Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- AIPro, an AI video analytics company, has released a free version of VistaPro, its fire and smoke detection monitoring software. The release allows facility operators to use basic functions with their existing CCTV cameras and PCs, confirm whether the software suits their actual site, and then add features as needed.

The free version can be downloaded from the AIPro official website (www.aipro.ai/download) without registration or login. The basic functions provided free of charge have no usage time limit. Users connect existing CCTV cameras that support RTSP video streaming to an Intel-based Windows PC that meets the recommended specifications, and the software runs without a separate high-performance graphics card.

The free version supports a total of three channels: one AI fire detection channel and two general monitoring channels. The fire detection channel analyzes flames and smoke, and video from multiple cameras can be viewed on a single screen. Detection history, statistics, and automatic reporting are also provided.

Real-time video analysis is performed on the user's PC. Both the free version (Free) and the paid Pro plan require an internet connection for updates and version management. Before installation, users can check the recommended PC specifications and CCTV integration requirements on the website.

The free distribution is designed so that users can verify CCTV compatibility and fire and smoke detection in their actual operating environment, and determine the features and operating scale their facilities need.

AIPro recommends first trying the software in a single area where fire risk needs to be monitored. Because camera angles, lighting, and work conditions differ from site to site, the company explained that it is important to review detection results at different times of day and decide on the operating approach accordingly. AI analysis results are used by managers to judge on-site conditions and the need for a response.

Real-time alerts, email notifications, and fire and map-based monitoring are provided in the paid Pro plan. AI detection channels can be added as needed, and a Business plan is available for companies and organizations that operate more cameras or need closed-network or site-specific configurations. Users start with the basic functions and then choose whether to expand according to their operating scale and purpose.

AIPro is an AI video analytics company founded in 2020 by Professor Cheon-Su Park of Sungkyunkwan University. It has built experience applying video analytics technology in the field for public institutions, including supplying fire and wildfire detection software to the Korea Asset Management Corporation.

AIPro believes that even small stores, warehouses, and workshops can evaluate the feasibility of AI safety management using their existing equipment. Going forward, the company plans to continue research to enhance fire and smoke detection performance and reduce false alarms, while improving ease of use from installation to reviewing detection results and managing records.

data.title: ROI-AI bust hurts Chinese stocks far more than GDP: Manishi Raychaudhuri
data.description:
HONG KONG, Nov 23 (Reuters) - The AI boom turbocharged China's export machine. A bust might not tank GDP, but it would be very bad news for China's equity market.

China's AI export boom has become an increasingly important support for the country's growth. Its global trade surplus topped $1 trillion in the first 10 months of 2026, driven by AI-related demand and weak domestic consumption. But a global AI spending slowdown or tighter US tech curbs could test the limits of Beijing's strategy.

China's equity investors thus find themselves in a quandary: sluggish domestic consumption and mounting export uncertainty are weighing on the outlook.

That predicament has been exacerbated by recent developments, including China's weak October retail sales, factory output and housing data, and the announcement of enhanced US restrictions on AI chip sales to China in the wake of the Nvidia ( NVDA ) scandal.

Former CEO Jensen Huang, who was ousted from the chip giant on November 12 for having multiple alleged affairs including with a suspected Chinese spy, was a prominent advocate for looser export controls, arguing that strict bans would only accelerate China's drive for technological self-reliance. His departure suggests the most recent curbs may be just the beginning.

Combined with investors' growing concerns about AI profitability, this raises the risk of a slowdown in US AI spending.

The potential impact on China's GDP would be significant - but not straightforward.

HIT FROM BOTH SIDES

China's dependence on AI-related exports was underscored in the third quarter. Net exports contributed almost 40% of gross domestic product (GDP) growth, and within Chinese merchandise exports, AI and technology-related goods occupy centre stage. The share of these goods climbed rapidly from an average of 25% of total exports over the decade through early 2025 to 33% by August 2026.

That might suggest that an AI slowdown could hit China's economic growth hard, but when calculating GDP, it is net exports - the value remaining after subtracting imports from exports - that matters, rather than gross exports alone.

This is a critical distinction because China's AI export model is heavily reliant on imported components. According to FactSet data, imports of technology-related products have skyrocketed amid the AI boom, rising to 37% of total Chinese imports over the past 14 months, after hovering around 25%-27% in the first half of 2025.

Those imports would probably also decline if AI spending faltered, meaning China's net exports could remain relatively protected, and the hit to GDP growth could be contained.

THE REAL RISK

What may worsen, however, is the US effort to contain China's technological progress, and that could have significant market impacts.

US-China relations appeared to have improved considerably this year, at least until a few weeks ago.

The US extended its trade truce with China to January 10, postponing punitive tariffs originally scheduled to take effect on November 10. Beijing mirrored the US pause by suspending its retaliatory 24% tariff applied broadly to all US-origin imported goods, and extending rare-earth and critical-mineral export waivers.

The two presidents, Donald Trump and Xi Jinping, have also met multiple times this year, most recently at last week's Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen. The mood was positive, as they appeared to largely sidestep the AI trade issue.

But the question of technology sharing clearly remains a sore point that has gotten a lot more painful with the Nvidia ( NVDA ) drama. Xi notably called out "trade protectionism" at the summit following the US chip curb announcement.

Further deterioration in US-China ties, alongside a potential slowdown in AI capital spending, could increase pressure on Beijing to stimulate domestic consumption, an approach it has long resisted as it prioritises manufacturing and technology self-reliance.

Yet China may resist making significant changes if it views the threat to GDP growth as limited, as my analysis suggests may be the case.

That could prolong tough times for Chinese equity investors, as they may be caught between a slowing domestic economy and vulnerable exports.

SLIM PICKINGS

No sector bet seems to be working in Chinese stocks this year. The semiconductor, tech hardware and robotics companies represented in the Shanghai STAR50 index, such as Cambricon Technologies, Semiconductor Manufacturing International Corp (SMIC) and Unitree Robotics , surged in the first half of 2026, only to collapse in the second half amid rising AI capex anxiety.

Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index, dominated by financials, consumers and industrials, and the mainland's CSI 300 Index , which is weighted toward technology hardware, financials, industrials and materials stocks, have performed no better.

China's domestic economy continues to be plagued by disorderly competition and declining margins, while technology exporters are now beleaguered by concerns about the robustness of their revenue.

In this environment, three areas stand out: policy-backed domestic champions, exporters with credible overseas supply chains, and selected biotech and drug-services companies that could benefit from surging global demand for specific molecules.

However, even here, the investment thesis is not always clear-cut. For example, market-leading household appliance, electric vehicle and battery manufacturers with overseas supply chains - such as Midea, Geely, BYD and CATL - could be relatively well positioned, yet most continue to face intense domestic competition, likely capping upside.

The situation could change, of course. Concerns about the health of the AI ecosystem could prove overblown. Or stringent US regulatory guardrails could inadvertently aid Chinese AI models. Absent such good fortune, however, an AI slowdown might simply harden Beijing's supply-side bias, leaving equity markets stuck.

(The views expressed here are those of Manishi Raychaudhuri, the founder and CEO of Emmer Capital Partners Ltd and the former head of Asia-Pacific equity research at BNP Paribas Securities.)

And listen to the Morning Bid daily podcast on Apple, Spotify, or the Reuters app. Subscribe to hear Reuters journalists discuss the biggest news in markets and finance seven days a week.

(Writing by Manishi Raychaudhuri; Editing by Marguerita Choy and Anna Szymanski)

data.title: OpenAI scientist proposes industry AI limits tied to model intelligence metric
data.description:
Nov 22 (Reuters) - AI developers should adopt common limits on increasingly powerful models and use "perplexity" as a common metric for measuring AI progress across the industry, OpenAI's chief scientist said on Sunday in a proposal backed by CEO Sam Altman.

The proposal detailed by OpenAI chief scientist Jakub Pachocki in a blog post was unveiled at a time of growing concern inside and outside the industry about the potential risks of AI's rapidly growing capabilities.

"I further propose common limits, based on perplexity and other measurements, that developers are committed to not crossing until our ability to understand and monitor AI behavior achieves a certain concrete milestone," Pachocki wrote.

Pachocki described perplexity as a model intelligence metric concerning how well a model predicts the next token - the basic unit of data - on average, and wrote that lower perplexity means better predictions.

Pachocki wrote that AI could help drive fundamental advances in AI training methods as soon as 2027, potentially accelerating progress more quickly than advances in monitoring and safety. Developers should commit to not cross agreed capability thresholds until new monitoring and safety mechanisms are in place, Pachocki said.

Pachocki advocated for an industry standard that specifies a first limit on development, and defines what milestones must be met before that limit is exceeded.

Altman backed the proposal, saying in a post on X that the industry should seek agreement on common limits for AI development. Altman described Pachocki's essay as "the most important thing OpenAI has published in awhile," and said such limits would help ensure safety and control.

(Reporting by Disha Mishra in Bengaluru; Editing by Will Dunham)

data.title: Beijing to bar young 'red-chip' firms from listing outside mainland China, sources say
data.description:
Nov 20 (Reuters) - China's securities watchdog has told some law firms it will not approve plans by red-chip firms to list outside mainland China, people familiar with the matter said, a move that tightens its control of capital raised offshore and could dent Hong Kong's IPO market.

Red-chip companies are registered abroad, mainly in tax havens, but control assets and businesses in China via equity ownership or contractual agreements.

The structure is favoured by Chinese startups, particularly tech firms, keen to raise capital in places like Hong Kong or New York to take advantage of more relaxed rules and deeper pools of funds available from foreign investors.

The China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC) has told law firm representatives in recent days that red-chip companies established after the introduction of new offshore listing rules in 2023 must be re-domiciled in China before they can list offshore, said the people.

The people declined to be identified as the regulatory guidance was confidential. The move is being reported for the first time by Reuters.

China and the US are competing fiercely to gain the upper hand in tech, particularly in AI and semiconductors, which has led to efforts by Chinese authorities to sharpen their scrutiny of technology, data and capital going outside its borders.

The CSRC did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment.

Oversight of red-chip firms has gradually become stricter.

Prior to March 2023, Chinese companies employing overseas holding structures to raise capital abroad did not need regulatory approval. That changed with the advent of the new rules.

Then this year, the CSRC told Reuters in March that it was examining the "necessity and compliance" of red-chip structures, particularly those formed after March 2023.

Despite that warning, some red-chip IPO hopefuls and their advisors have been seeking approval to list outside the mainland without dismantling their existing structure and shifting their domicile back to China, one of the people said.

Most of those applicants failed to convince the regulator that a red-chip structure was necessary, prompting the tougher stance, the person added.

HONG KONG IPO MARKET COULD BE HURT

A drop-off in listings from red-chip firms is likely to hurt but not hobble Hong Kong, the top IPO destination for Chinese firms, which has seen business boom for the past 18 months.

Funds raised via IPOs in Hong Kong during the first 10 months of this year surged 84% from the same period last year to hit HK$404 billion ($52 billion), though the CSRC has slowed approvals of IPOs since September.

In addition to going slow on approvals for listings by AI, chip and humanoid robot firms after a market frenzy in those sectors, it has more broadly increased its scrutiny as markets have weakened.

Last year, one-fifth of 131 Hong Kong listings approved by the CSRC involved offshore holdings, the majority of which used a red-chip structure, according to Chinese law firm Han Kun.

So far this year, the CSRC has approved Hong Kong listings for just 6 red-chip companies, a sharp decline from 50 approved last year, according to data compiled by law firms and Reuters.

There were nearly 600 listing applications pending in Hong Kong at the end of October, official data showed.

Most of them are mainland Chinese firms though it was not clear how many are red chips given that the number includes applications that were filed confidentially.

There are, however, at least four active Hong Kong IPO applicants which have an offshore holding company structure for their mainland China businesses, according to a Reuters review of filings with the Hong Kong stock exchange.

Any red-chip firms seeking to list in Hong Kong or New York could now face a long wait before coming to market due to the time and costs involved in becoming incorporated in China.

But some, like Chinese AI firm StepFun, have been working on shifting their domicile back to China to pave the way for a planned overseas listing, sources have said. StepFun did not respond to a Reuters request for comment.

Asked about news of the ban on red-chip firms listing outside mainland China, the Hong Kong bourse said it "welcomes issuers with a range of ownership structures, provided they meet all applicable regulatory requirements in Hong Kong and other relevant jurisdictions."

($1 = 7.8410 Hong Kong dollars)

(Reporting by Reuters staff; Editing by Edwina Gibbs)

data.title: Trump to welcome investors at gala for his plunging meme coin
data.description:
NEW YORK, Nov 22 (Reuters) - US President Donald Trump will headline his third meme coin gala on Sunday night at his country club outside Washington, DC, for top holders of the tokens, which were once worth about $75 each but are now valued at less than $1.

Less than 20 months after the first $TRUMP token gala set off a frenzy among 220 wealthy crypto holders vying for spots at the dinner with the president, interest has waned for the latest affair at the Trump National club in Sterling, Virginia.

Organizers indicated that 185 crypto wallets qualified for the dinner, although the leaderboard on the $TRUMP coin club website listed just 130 wallets when the contest concluded on November 16. Together, those listed wallets only held $8.6 million - a shadow of the $148 million listed for the first dinner in May 2025, when a time-weighted holding of $18.5 million grabbed the top seat.

According to the contest's website, the top 29 winners - which had the highest time-weighted holdings during the contest scoring period from September 30 to November 16 - will join a VIP reception with the president and receive a gift bag with Trump swag. The top four also get an 18-karat gold Trump-branded watch.

Trump and his family have monetized his brand through an array of equities and crypto ventures during his foray into politics.

More than half of the digital wallets publicly listed on the contest leaderboard for Sunday's dinner are tied directly to crypto exchanges that bar US-based users, indicating they are linked to foreign nationals, according to an analysis of blockchain data prepared for Reuters by the nonpartisan, nonprofit consumer advocacy group Public Citizen. 

Democratic leaders in the House and the Senate, where the party won a resounding victory in the midterm elections, have vowed to investigate what they say are unprecedented conflicts of interest posed by the Trump family's business dealings during Trump's presidency. They also say they plan to push for legislation that would ban such activities. 

The Trump Meme Coin project and the White House did not respond to requests for comment, although the Trump administration has long said the president's business interests are clean.

"Neither the President nor his family has ever engaged - or will ever engage - in conflicts of interest," White House spokesperson Anna Kelly told Reuters earlier this year. "President Trump proudly made the United States the crypto capital of the world through executive actions."

The Trump family's other crypto-connected equities and ventures have also fallen in value to record lows. Together, outside investors in their five main crypto and crypto-linked projects have lost more than $5 billion, according to a Reuters analysis. 

The Trump meme coin has earned the Trump family at least $635 million, according to the president's June financial disclosure statement. In total, the Trumps had earned at least $2.3 billion through April from their four main crypto ventures, including the meme coin.

The president's stake in a fifth crypto-linked venture, Trump Media & Technology Group ( DJT ), is worth about $430 million.

(Reporting by Michelle Conlin in New York; Editing by Sergio Non and Edmund Klamann)

data.title: Soccer-Legacy key for 2031 and 2035 Women's World Cup says sports executive
data.description:
* Former Football Australia CEO James Johnson says World Cup hosts must prioritise legacy from day one

* FIFA to confirm the United States, Jamaica, Costa Rica and Mexico as 2031 Women's World Cup hosts

* Johnson says the expanded 48-team format can amplify host-nation exposure and grow the women's game

* Johnson welcomes Netflix's ( NFLX ) World Cup involvement but warns against limiting access through paywalls

By Iain Axon

CALGARY, Canada, Nov 22 (Reuters) - Focusing on the legacy of the Women's World Cup should be the top priority for those organising the 2031 and 2035 tournaments, according to a sports executive behind the 2023 competition.

In Zurich on Monday, FIFA will confirm that the United States, Jamaica, Costa Rica and Mexico will host in 2031, with England, Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland on co-hosting duties in 2035.

Unlike Australia and New Zealand in 2023, there will be 48 teams rather than 32, streaming giant Netflix ( NFLX ) will have some involvement and the tournaments will be held in markets more mature in terms of women's soccer development than Australia.

But for James Johnson, who was the CEO for Football Australia between 2020 and 2025 and is now the commissioner of the Canadian Premier League, legacy remains the fundamental driving force administrators should be thinking about.

"If you're focused on legacy, I think it helps the tournament," he told Reuters by Zoom from Calgary, Canada, after writing a book on his 2023 experience, "Hosting the World".

"In Australia it was about moving the sport from a fourth, fifth or even sixth-tier sport into the mainstream, and we were able to accomplish that.

"It is a different market for 2031 and 2035. But the legacy conversation starts as soon as the hosting is officially awarded to those countries."

An imperative for Johnson in 2023 was that the Matildas made it to the last weekend of the tournament, something he ensured by fighting for long-term funding for the team.

Getting to the third-placed playoff meant many weeks of exposure for women's soccer in a country more traditionally interested in cricket and rugby.

'BETTER OPPORTUNITIES'

And although it has received some criticism elsewhere for diluting quality, Johnson believes the expansion to 48 teams for 2031 and 2035 provides an opportunity for the host countries to spend more time in the limelight.

"The additional content, the additional matches, what I hope it translates into is better opportunities for the home teams because that's really the amplifier of culture and the amplifier of interest in the tournaments," he said.

"A host nation taking the tournament by storm and staying in there from start to finish is a key for the success of the tournament - and the cultural impact you create as a result."

Next year's Women's World Cup in Brazil will include the involvement of a major streamer for the first time, with Netflix ( NFLX ) securing rights in the US and Canada for that tournament and the 2031 competition, as well as expressing interest in the 2030 men's World Cup.

Ahead of the 2023 World Cup FIFA were critical of some traditional broadcasters - especially in Europe - for what they said was an undervaluation of women's soccer.

But while Johnson welcomed the arrival of Netflix ( NFLX ), he cautioned against the long-term danger of locking out potential viewers who had previously watched on free-to-air.

"It creates a new dynamic, it's interesting, it's healthy for the sport because there's more competitions," he said.

"What I hope it doesn't do though is put too much content behind paywalls because I think the beauty of a World Cup is the community that it creates, and the buzz that it creates, and the ability to bring people together, which means it needs to be widely distributed."

(Reporting by Iain Axon in London; Editing by Christian Radnedge)

data.title: Soccer-Pochettino backs Man United players after Liverpool thrashing, rejects relegation talk
data.description:
* Pochettino says eighth-minute red card left side with impossible task

* United boss insists players showed fight despite 4-0 loss

* Former United captain Keane blasts applauding fans after Anfield humiliation

By Lori Ewing

LIVERPOOL, England, Nov 22 (Reuters) - Mauricio Pochettino insisted Manchester United's ( MANU ) players had shown fight and commitment despite a humiliating 4-0 defeat at Liverpool in his first game in charge, rejecting suggestions the club's dire start to the season pointed towards a relegation battle.

United remain 19th in the Premier League table with one win from 11 games after a crushing loss at Anfield on Sunday, where Leny Yoro's eighth-minute red card left the visitors facing an uphill struggle for more than 80 minutes.

"We need to accept the reality and we need to be responsible, we need to be united, we need to be all together," Pochettino said, when asked what he had learned about the size of the task facing him.

"What I learned from my players is that they like to fight, they commit with the team, with the club, and of course they want to win games. They want to make the effort.

"Today was a test that, for me, is very positive. After eight minutes, 10 men, red card, concede the goal in this action and then 80 minutes to play. Do you think that it's easy?"

The defeat was the joint heaviest for a United manager in his first match in charge, according to Opta, equalling the 4-0 loss to Bolton Wanderers suffered by Lal Hilditch in 1926.

The Argentine, who was hired after the sacking of Michael Carrick and arrived in Manchester only on Wednesday after a stint with the United States national team, said the dismissal of Yoro fundamentally altered the contest and repeatedly returned to the sending-off when assessing his side's performance.

"Even the best team in the world playing like this in this situation, in our circumstance, maybe concede four goals or maybe more."

Pochettino also questioned the decision itself, arguing that Liverpool striker Alexander Isak did not have the ball under control when Yoro brought him down.

'APPLAUDING RUBBISH'

Former United captain Roy Keane was among those unimpressed by attempts to find positives in the defeat, questioning why the United supporters still in the stadium at the final whistle applauded the players.

"Fans are applauding the players, applauding what? Applauding rubbish," Keane said. "When do the players take responsibility for some of the decision making?

"Liverpool should have scored eight or nine. I feel like swearing."

Pochettino, however, refused to dwell on criticism or wider questions about United's defensive record after the team conceded four goals for the third time this season across all competitions.

"It's painful because it's 4-0 at the end and you lose the game. But you need to (consider) the circumstances," he said. "We are not going to lose more than one game how we lose today. We have a lot of work to do."

With a Champions League trip to Portugal to face Sporting on Wednesday, Pochettino said his message in the dressing room was simple.

"They are very, very, very low," he said. "But I said, 'head up, and we need to keep working, be concentrated, try to go to Portugal and try to win the game'."

(Reporting by Lori Ewing Editing by Toby Davis)

data.title: Wall St Week Ahead-'Black Friday' brings consumer spending into focus for AI-rocked market
data.description:
* Anthropic IPO, solid Nvidia ( NVDA ) earnings fail to lift market

* Holiday retail sales seen up 4.2%, per Oxford Economics

* Consumer spending in focus in light of higher prices, energy costs

By Lewis Krauskopf

NEW YORK, Nov 20 (Reuters) - Investors next week will focus on consumer spending, looking for evidence that a broadly solid economy can help calm a US stock market unsettled by doubts about the AI trade.

The S&P 500 and the Dow tumbled on Friday, confirming they were in a correction, while Anthropic shares retreated after a blockbuster debut that had raised hopes of easing worries about an AI trade already roiled by valuation concerns.

Next week, "Black Friday" heralds the onrush of the holiday shopping season as retailers offer a wave of discounts. Investors will watch for signs of how consumers are coping with inflation, including rising energy and borrowing costs. Consumer spending accounts for roughly two-thirds of the US economy.

"If you continue to see a strong consumer, it should help to lift the economy," said Jim Baird, chief investment officer with Plante Moran Financial Advisors. "That directly contributes back to stronger corporate revenue and earnings growth, and provides a catalyst for investors that extends beyond the AI trade and to other parts of the economy."

Investors are still digesting a steep pullback in heavyweight technology and AI stocks.

This week, the blockbuster market debut from Claude creator Anthropic and a solid quarterly report from beleaguered AI chipmaker Nvidia ( NVDA ) failed to steady the stock market. Spurred by concerns about heavy financing needs and political pushback, doubts have emerged about the massive spending on data centers and other AI infrastructure that has underpinned the 4-year-old bull market.

"Markets and investors are looking at the tech sector with a lot more questions," said Paul Nolte, senior wealth adviser and market strategist at Murphy & Sylvest Wealth Management.

The Anthropic IPO offered investors their first chance to invest in a publicly traded AI lab, and the stock's performance was expected to drive broad sentiment in coming days. Anthropic's shares opened sharply higher on their first day of trading, then pared gains and closed up 17% on Thursday, while major stock indexes sank. On Friday, Anthropic fell 9%.

The S&P 500 has fallen 11.6% from its October 6 all-time high, dragged down by the technology sector, which has slumped nearly 24.7% in that time.

A recent series of technology snafus that disrupted areas from banking to travel to email also left investors edgy heading into a US trading week that will be shortened due to the Thanksgiving holiday.

SOLID OCTOBER RETAIL SALES SETTING HOLIDAY TONE?

Weakness in stocks could threaten consumers' holiday gift-buying, if they feel less wealthy and less likely to spend.

Oxford Economics estimates that holiday retail sales will rise 4.2%, or an increase of 2.2% in volume after adjusting for inflation. That covers retail spending in November and December, excluding autos, gasoline, and bars and restaurants.

The National Retail Federation projects 182.7 million consumers plan to shop this year during the five-day Thanksgiving period that runs to "Cyber Monday", citing results from a recent survey. Black Friday is expected to be the most popular day to shop during that period. That overall number would be down slightly from 186.9 million last year, but continues the trend of elevated shopping during the holiday weekend in recent years, the NRF said.

Government data this week showed US retail sales for October increased moderately, while the core measure of such sales rose faster than expected. Retailers including Walmart ( WMT ) and Target ( TGT ) had upbeat comments or outlooks for the holiday season in their quarterly reports this week.

"The consumer is pretty healthy, and we'd like to see that continue through the end of the year," Nolte said.

COULD GASOLINE PRICES SAP SHOPPING?

Despite solid retail sales data, Gene Goldman, chief investment officer at Cetera Financial Group, said he was worried "that the consumer is being impacted by higher gas prices, higher energy prices, higher food prices."

The average national price for a gallon of gasoline stood at $3.69 on Friday, according to motorists' group AAA. That is down from about $4.28 a month ago, but well above the $3.10 level a year ago.

As the holiday shopping season heats up, Goldman said he was watching the extent of shopping done in stores compared to online, and how much consumers are buying necessities versus discretionary items.

"If the economy exceeds expectations, earnings increase, and earnings drive stock prices," Goldman said.

Investors in the coming week also will monitor reports on inflation and consumer confidence along with an updated read on third-quarter US GDP. Quarterly results are due from Dell Technologies ( DELL ) and semiconductor company Analog Devices ( ADI ) , which could sway the AI and tech trade.

With just over a month left in 2026, the S&P 500 is on track for a year-to-date gain of about 1%. The index has fallen for seven straight sessions, the longest such streak since February 2020. This week it dropped below its 200-day moving average -- a closely watched trendline that acts as a support level for buyers -- for the first time since April.

"There is a lot to like about the fundamentals" of the market, said Mark Hackett, chief market strategist for Nationwide. "But picking bottoms is difficult when the market is so emotional."

(Reporting by Lewis Krauskopf; Additional reporting by Saqib Iqbal Ahmed; editing by Colin Barr, David Gregorio and David Gaffen)

data.title: Bitcoin's quantum security challenge extends to bridges, custodians and millions of coins
data.description:
Bitcoin faces a problem that stronger cryptography alone cannot solve: moving millions of coins to quantum-resistant security while upgrading the exchanges, custodians and bridges that handle them.

Some blockchains have begun introducing quantum-resistant security. NEAR added post-quantum transaction signing in July, while Algorand introduced native Falcon-1024 accounts in August.

Millions of bitcoin (BTC) remain in wallets secured by older signatures, and exchanges, custodians and bridges would need to make their own changes to protect the funds they handle.

“The clock that matters is migration,” said Leo Fan, CEO of blockchain infrastructure company Cysic.

For bitcoin holders, moving funds to stronger security may become necessary long before quantum computers can break existing signatures. But dormant coins could remain exposed, and institutions holding or transferring bitcoin would have to upgrade their systems as well.

Exposed public keys

More than 6 million bitcoin, representing 31.2% of circulating supply, were held behind public keys already visible onchain in October, according to Glassnode data.

Those coins are safe for now, but a quantum computer powerful enough to break today's cryptography could use exposed public keys to gain control of the funds.

The figures illustrate the size of the migration challenge. They do not establish how many coins are lost, dormant or impossible to move.

Bitcoin developers are already debating what should happen to holdings that fail to migrate.

In April, developer Jameson Lopp and five co-authors proposed Bitcoin Improvement Proposal 361, which would phase out vulnerable signature methods and eventually restrict transactions from wallets that had not upgraded.

Lopp argued that freezing dormant bitcoin could be preferable to allowing future quantum attackers to steal it.

Blockstream CEO Adam Back favored voluntary upgrades, warning against forcing holders to migrate through a predetermined freeze.

Neither approach has been adopted. BIP 361 remains a draft, as does BIP 360, which proposes a new Bitcoin output type designed to reduce exposure to certain quantum attacks.

“Coins that never move are a social problem, not a technical one,” Fan said.

His concern is that developers can introduce new security standards, but they cannot necessarily compel wallet owners to adopt them.

“If the old path stays open forever, attackers will use it,” he said.

Bridges and custody

The same problem affects crypto custodians, which often require multiple parties to approve transactions rather than relying on a single private key. These systems would also need to be changed to support quantum-resistant signatures.

“Post-quantum signatures for a single signer are standardized, but threshold and multisig versions are still at the research stage,” Fan said.

The U.S. National Institute of Standards and Technology issued a call for multi-party threshold cryptography proposals in January, reflecting ongoing work.

In May, BitGo ( BTGO ) and Silence Laboratories completed a simulated post-quantum transaction using multi-party computation, a system that distributes control of private keys.

The demonstration showed how the technology could work in institutional custody, although the companies have not announced a production deployment.

Bridges connecting Bitcoin to other blockchains face similar complications because their security depends on systems operating across different networks.

Rootstock, a Bitcoin sidechain, has outlined plans to introduce quantum-resistant signatures in 2028. Its roadmap also includes changes to PowPeg, the bridge that secures bitcoin on Rootstock, and work on hardware security modules and Bitcoin-side protections.

Those changes remain proposals, and Rootstock cannot independently upgrade Bitcoin's underlying protocol.

For custodians and bridge operators, implementing new signatures will require changes to the systems that control funds, some of which depend on networks they do not operate.

For Bitcoin holders, the consequences could be more direct: those who cannot or do not migrate may eventually face restrictions on moving their coins, or leave them vulnerable to future attacks.

data.title: South Korea prepares market stabilisation funds after KOSPI hits 10-month low

SEOUL, Nov 22 (Reuters) - South Korea will be ready to deploy market stabilisation funds immediately should conditions continue to deteriorate, the finance ministry said on Sunday, after the country's benchmark stock index slumped last week to a 10-month low.

"Preparation work on necessary measures... will immediately begin so that securities market stabilisation funds can be activated immediately depending on market conditions," the ministry said in a statement, after minister Lee Hyoung-il held an emergency meeting with other economic policymakers.

On Friday, the benchmark KOSPI stock index dropped more than 5% to close at its lowest level since January 16, as shares in Anthropic fizzled after their market debut amid general concerns about AI and tech valuations.

The Korean index has fallen more than 40% from its June peak after more than doubling in value in the first half in a world-beating rally, led by chipmakers Samsung Electronics ( SSNLF ) and SK Hynix ( SKHY ).

STABILISATION FUNDS

Among other market stabilising measures, the meeting attendees agreed to temporarily loosen for three months regulations on the daily limit of stock repurchases by listed companies, to help ease market volatility.

They also agreed to closely monitor leveraged investments and margin calls to ease selling pressure and respond to illegal short-selling and other market-disturbing behaviour.

The measures come after financial authorities in Taiwan on Saturday ordered a further tightening of short-selling rules for stocks, while its finance ministry said its $15 billion stock stabilisation fund had already entered the market to support prices and maintain stability.

South Korea has rarely spent its securities market stabilising funds and has mostly used them as a tool to calm investor sentiment, including during the COVID-19 pandemic.

(Reporting by Jihoon Lee; Edting by Kate Mayberry and David Holmes)

data.title: Chinese exchanges ease margin trading requirements to aid stock markets

SHANGHAI, Nov 22 (Reuters) - China's three main stock exchanges announced plans to aid struggling share prices with a batch of measures such as easing requirements for margin financing.

In addition, the Shanghai and Shenzhen bourses unveiled plans for fee reductions to lower trading costs, while the Shenzhen exchange also proposed to introduce a market-making mechanism in its startup board ChiNext.

The moves came after Beijing unveiled measures in early November to encourage share purchases as equities struggle amid sluggish growth at home, a global selloff in AI stocks and rising geopolitical tensions.

The benchmark Shanghai Composite Index dropped nearly 3% last week to hit a 16-month low. Shanghai's tech-heavy STAR Market and Shenzhen's ChiNext have both tumbled more than 40% from their June peaks.

REGULATORY CHANGES

The Chinese measures come as other Asian markets including South Korea and Taiwan respond to stock market jitters with regulatory changes designed to steady volatility.

Under the new rules announced by the Shanghai, Shenzhen and Beijing exchanges, investors can borrow more money to buy stocks against the same collateral.

Starting November 30, the minimum margin ratio would be cut to 80% from 100% previously, in a reversal of a policy announced in January.

"Margin financing activity has weakened significantly recently, while overall leverage is low," the three exchanges said in identical statements.

The cut in margin requirements "would improve market liquidity and support the market's long-term stability and healthy development."

MEASURES AIM TO BOOST MARKET CONFIDENCE

The level of China's outstanding margin loans has dropped more than 20% to roughly 2.2 trillion yuan ($329.49 billion), from a peak of 3 trillion yuan in late June.

Separately, the Shanghai and Shenzhen exchanges announced fee cuts aiming to lower trading costs, boost market confidence and invigorate the market.

The Shenzhen bourse also published draft rules to introduce market-making mechanisms in a bid to "curb share price swings, improve pricing efficiency and strengthen market resilience".
